1.5.rationale: In the Indonesian source, “kekerasan” is defined in Pasal 1 angka 14 as abuse of physical force causing suffering “secara fisik, psikis, seksual, dan/atau penelantaran” (physical, psychological, sexual, and/or neglect). It does not explicitly include “kekerasan ekonomi” (economic violence) as a violence category. The text does mention economic loss as part of the victim’s suffering (Pasal 1 angka 9–10: suffering includes “ekonomi”) and defines “eksploitasi” as including extortion and obtaining material benefit (Pasal 1 angka 15), and it provides protection of victims’ assets (Penjelasan Pasal 8 huruf e; Penjelasan Pasal 9 huruf g). However, these are not framed as “economic violence” as a distinct form of violence; they are framed as economic harm/loss and exploitation/property protection. Therefore the judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the document, and the golden ‘Yes’ likely over-interprets the presence of economic loss/property protection as an explicit economic-violence category.

1.6.evaluator_rationale: None of the candidate sentences mention harmful practices such as early/child marriage, female genital mutilation, honour crimes, or female infanticide.

CHAPTER III
RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
Part One
Rights of Female Victims

Article 17
(1) Regional Government provides comprehensive protection to women from various actions:
a. threats;
b. Discrimination;
c. Violence; and
d. Exploitation.
(2) Every form of threatening action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, whether verbal or non-verbal, that is intentionally directed at women so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(3) Every form of Discrimination action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b that is carried out leading to gender, racial, or equality injustice so as to degrade the status, freedom and opportunities of women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(4) Every form of Violence action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c that is carried out whether physical, psychological, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(5) Every form of Exploitation action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d that is carried out in any form that degrades the dignity, honor, and respect of women and causes harm to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Purworejo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Purworejo.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
6. Village is a village and customary village or called by another name, hereinafter referred to as Village, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage governmental affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia and located in Purworejo Regency.
7. Village Government is the Village Head or called by another name who is assisted by village apparatus as an element of Village Government administration.
8. Sub-district is part of the territory of the District as a District apparatus.
9. Female Victim is a woman who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses caused by violence, exploitation and/or gender-based discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life.
10. Child Victim is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses caused by violence, exploitation and/or discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life.
11. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion either direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
14. Violence is any act of abuse of physical force with or without using means, unlawfully and causing misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
15. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or Services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
16. Child Maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over children, who should be trusted, namely parents, close family, teachers, coaches, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions.
17. Prevention is all efforts to prevent Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation, as well as recurrence of occurrences against Women and Children.
18. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect which includes complaint Services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution.
19. Assistance is all efforts and actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-strengthening of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect of Women and Children to resolve problems faced so as to provide a sense of security and comfort and have readiness and/or ability to obtain Services and live their lives.
20. Assistant is a person or group or organization that is trusted and/or has skills and knowledge to assist Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation with the aim that Female Victims and Child Victims feel safe and comfortable in accessing Services.
21. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Maltreatment, neglect and other problems.
22. Forum for the Protection of Violence Victims hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for Prevention, handling and empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Violence and other problems whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and established at the Regional, District, and Village levels.
23. Integrated Service Center is a non-structural institution that coordinates the implementation of an integrated Service system for Female Victims and Child Victims.
24. Social Reintegration is all efforts to strengthen the readiness and ability of Female Victims and Child Victims to regain their welfare in social, political, economic, and cultural life with dignity, including strengthening acceptance and support into the family and/or community environment for the protection and fulfillment of the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims.
25. Restitution is compensation payment given to Female Victims, Child Victims and/or victims' families by the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by Female Victims, Child Victims and/or victims' families.
26. Legal Aid Provider is a legal aid institution or community organization that provides legal aid services based on laws and regulations.
27. Business World is a commercial organization, the entire industrial environment and production of goods/services, including State-Owned Enterprises, and Regional-Owned Enterprises as well as private or entrepreneurs and their networks, who will carry out their social responsibilities.

Article 26
(1) Female Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, mistreatment, and/or neglect who experience trauma shall undergo a gradual rehabilitation process both physically, psychologically, and socially.
(2) Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
(3) The Regional Government shall guarantee the fulfillment of living needs of Female Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, mistreatment, and/or neglect during the rehabilitation process.

1.6.rationale: The Indonesian policy explicitly addresses a classic ‘harmful practice’: child/early marriage. Pasal 14 huruf e states parents/guardians’ responsibility includes “mencegah perkawinan di usia anak” (prevent marriage at child age). That is direct evidence for harmful practices (early/child marriage). The judge said none of the candidates mention early/child marriage, but the retrieved candidates for this indicator did include Article 14 in English under a different discrepancy set (and in this document it exists clearly in Indonesian). This suggests the evaluation/judge decision for 1.6 was made without considering the relevant provision (or the retrieval set for 1.6 missed Pasal 14 even though it is the key evidence). Given the provided 1.6 candidate list indeed lacks Pasal 14, the immediate pipeline failure is retrieval; however, based strictly on the discrepancy package shown, the judge’s rationale matches the (incomplete) candidates. So the core issue is that the system failed to surface Pasal 14(e) for this indicator.

5.2.rationale: The Indonesian text includes explicit religious/spiritual service elements: Pasal 33 ayat (2) huruf d provides “Pendamping di bidang mental spiritual keagamaan” (assistants in mental-spiritual religious matters) for child victims, and Pasal 41 ayat (1) huruf f includes “Pelayanan kerohanian” (spiritual services) as part of the Integrated Service Center.
